content.text: This section aims to keep Eduversal Partner Schools' status as approved Cambridge Assessment International Education Centres. It also aims to protect examination integrity, deliver high-quality Cambridge curriculum and assessments, and follow all Cambridge policies and procedures.
A Cambridge Centre is a school or institution approved by Cambridge Assessment International Education to:

items: Deliver Cambridge curriculum (Primary, Lower Secondary, IGCSE, AS & A Level)
Register students for Cambridge examinations
Run Cambridge exams under secure and standardized conditions
Receive official Cambridge certificates and results
content.title: What is a Cambridge Centre?

content.text: Centre Number: Each Eduversal Partner School has its own unique Cambridge Centre number. Cambridge International issues this number, and it is shown on the Centre certificate. The number identifies the school in all Cambridge systems and correspondence.
Initial Application (for new schools joining the Eduversal network):

items: The school must hold a valid Indonesian operational license
Adequate facilities (classrooms, labs, exam rooms)
Qualified teaching staff
Commitment to Cambridge standards and ethics
Complete the Cambridge Centre application on the Cambridge International Direct website
Provide school details, staffing, and facilities information
Name the people for the key roles: Centre Head (Principal) and Exams Officer
Pay application fee (one-time)
Cambridge reviews the application. Cambridge may ask for extra information or a site visit
Approval typically takes 4-8 weeks
After approval, the school receives the Centre number and login details for the Cambridge systems.
Centre status has no end date, as long as the school keeps meeting the ongoing requirements

content.text: Existing Centres: All established Eduversal Partner Schools already hold Cambridge Centre status. The school principal keeps this status active. The principal maintains the registration, updates Centre details, and meets the annual requirements.
Requirement: Every year, each Centre must complete an Annual Centre Declaration and submit it to Cambridge. The declaration confirms that:

items: Centre contact details are current (address, phone, email)
Key staff details (Centre Head, Exams Officer) are up to date, and the Quality Nominee post is filled
Facilities are still suitable for running exams
The Centre commits to keeping Cambridge standards and exam security
content.title: Annual Centre Declaration

items: Cambridge sends the declaration form (usually February-March)
Deadline: Before exam entry windows open (varies by series)
The Exams Officer prepares the declaration, and the Centre Head (Principal) signs it. The declaration is submitted online through Cambridge International Direct

content.text: Failure to Complete: Not submitting the declaration may lead to suspension of Centre status or to the school being unable to register students for exams. Evidence:

items: Cambridge Centre number certificate
Annual declaration submission confirmations (past 3 years)
Correspondence with Cambridge about Centre status

content.text: Cambridge requires each Centre to name specific people who are responsible for examination integrity and quality assurance.

items: Overall accountability for Cambridge Centre compliance
Make sure exams are run securely, and prevent malpractice
Approve student registrations and exam entries
Give final approval on examination results and on any irregularities
Communicate with Cambridge about Centre matters
Make sure staff understand and follow Cambridge policies
content.title: Centre Head (Principal - Primary or Secondary School Principal)

items: Makes the final decision at Centre level on Cambridge-related issues
May give day-to-day tasks to the Exams Officer, but keeps final responsibility

content.text:
Appointment: The Centre Head appoints a dedicated staff member to manage examination operations. This is often the Administrative Manager, Vice Principal, or a senior teacher.

Responsibilities: Before Exams:

items: Coordinate exam entries (student registration, subject selection, tier decisions)
Submit entries to Cambridge through Cambridge International Direct by the deadlines.
Order secure exam materials (question papers, answer booklets, CDs/USBs)
Plan the exam timetable (solve clashes for students who take more than one exam)
Arrange exam rooms, seating plans, and invigilation schedules
Train invigilators on the Cambridge exam conduct rules
Communicate exam schedules and instructions to students and parents
content.title: Exams Officer

items: Supervise the secure storage of exam materials (locked safe/cabinet; controlled access)
Deliver exam papers to the exam room just before each exam starts
Monitor exam conduct and respond to irregularities (student illness, disruption, suspected malpractice)
Collect completed scripts and keep them secure until dispatch
Package and dispatch scripts to Cambridge (or upload them for e-marking, if this applies)
Submit attendance registers and any incident reports
Tell students their results when Cambridge releases them
Manage post-results services (enquiries about results, access to scripts, appeals)

Archive exam documents according to the consolidated retention schedule in 14.5. That schedule gives the period and the legal basis for each record type. Cambridge links retention to events rather than to one fixed period (for example, keep delivery and printing records until certificates are received). Do not apply a single blanket figure
Cambridge provides online training modules and resources for Exams Officers
The Exams Officer must keep up to date with Cambridge Handbook changes and attend Eduversal network training sessions
Exams Officer appointment letter
Training completion certificates (Cambridge online modules, Eduversal sessions)
Exam administration checklists and logs (entries, materials, dispatch)
Invigilation schedules and training records

content.text:
Purpose: The Quality Nominee supports internal quality assurance and leads the school's work on examination standards and curriculum delivery.

Appointment: Usually a senior academic leader (Principal, Vice Principal Academic, or Head of Department (HOD)) who understands the Cambridge curriculum and assessment well.

Responsibilities:

items: Check teaching quality and curriculum coverage against the Cambridge standards.
Review student work and assessment practices to check that they match Cambridge expectations.
Facilitate internal moderation and standardization
Identify professional development needs for Cambridge curriculum delivery
Communicate with Cambridge about curriculum updates, resources, and support
Take part in Cambridge training and quality assurance activities (e.g., webinars, regional meetings)
content.title: Quality Nominee

items: Quality Nominee appointment letter
Meeting notes on curriculum review and quality assurance
Internal moderation records
Participation in Cambridge professional development events

content.text: Eduversal Partner Schools deliver the Cambridge curriculum in several stages. Each stage fits the students' age and progress.

items: Subjects: English, Mathematics, Science
Skills-based approach with clear learning objectives
Strong focus on inquiry, problem-solving, and application
content.title: Cambridge Primary (Ages 5-11)

items: Cambridge Primary Checkpoint: Optional diagnostic tests at the end of Primary (usually Grade 6, age 11)
Tests in English, Mathematics, Science
Gives a feedback report that compares student performance with international benchmarks
Not high-stakes; used for formative purposes (to support learning) and to plan the move to Lower Secondary
Cambridge Primary subjects are taught in English, with EAL support when needed
Indonesian national subjects are taught separately (Bahasa Indonesia, PPKn, Religion, Mulok)
Profil Pelajar Pancasila projects and character education are integrated
Subjects: English, Mathematics, Science (core); extra subjects may include ICT, Global Perspectives, Art, Music, PE
Builds on Primary; deepens understanding of concepts and skills
content.title: Cambridge Lower Secondary (Ages 11-14)

items: Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint: diagnostic tests at the end of Lower Secondary (end of Grade 8, age 13-14), marked outside the school. They are optional under Cambridge rules, but every Eduversal partner school is expected to run them
Tests in English, Mathematics, Science
Provides diagnostic feedback and readiness for IGCSE
Cambridge Lower Secondary as a foundation for IGCSE progression
Students continue Indonesian national subjects to meet MoE (Ministry of Education) requirements
International General Certificate of Secondary Education
Recognized around the world as equal to national secondary qualifications (e.g., UK GCSE, US Grade 10-11 completion)
Many subjects available (70+ subjects; schools choose based on capacity and student interest)
content.title: Cambridge IGCSE (Ages 14-16, Grades 9-10)

content.text:
Typical Subject Offering at Eduversal Schools:

Core Subjects (Required for most students):

items: English as a Second Language (ESL) or English Literature
Mathematics (Core or Extended tier)
Sciences: Biology, Chemistry, Physics (separate sciences or Combined Science)

content.text: Extra Subjects (Student choice based on interest and university plans):

items: Humanities: Geography, History, Global Perspectives
Languages: Indonesian as a First Language, Mandarin, French (varies by school)
Business & Economics: Business Studies, Economics, Accounting
Creative & Technical: Art & Design, ICT, Computer Science, Design & Technology
Other: Physical Education, Music
Grades: A* (highest), A, B, C, D, E, F, G, U (ungraded/fail)
A new 9-1 grading scale is used for some subjects (9 = A* (highest), 4 = C-equivalent, 1 = G)
The network default is six IGCSE subjects over two years (Grades 9-10). Any lower load is a documented exception made after academic review
Mainly external exams at the end of the two-year course (May/June series in Grade 10)
Some subjects include a coursework component (submitted during the course; externally moderated by Cambridge)
Tiered exams for some subjects (e.g., Mathematics Core vs Extended)
Advanced Subsidiary (AS) Level: the Eduversal standard for completing the program is four AS Level examinations (three pathway subjects plus one shared critical-thinking component)
A Level: Two-year course, usually 3-4 subjects (may include AS as first year)
Depth and difficulty similar to first-year university in some countries
content.title: Cambridge AS & A Level (Ages 16-18, Grades 11-12)

items: Sciences: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, Further Mathematics
Humanities: History, Geography, Economics, Psychology, Sociology
Languages: English Language, English Literature, Indonesian
Business: Business, Accounting
Other: Art & Design, Computer Science, ICT
AS Level: Grades a, b, c, d, e (lowercase, to show they are different from A Level grades)
A Level: Grades A* (highest), A, B, C, D, E, U (ungraded)
Mainly external exams (May/June or October/November series)
Some subjects include practical exams (Sciences) or coursework (Art, certain humanities)
Cambridge AS/A Levels are widely recognized for university admission around the world
Competitive Indonesian universities increasingly accept A Levels
UK, Australia, Canada, US, Europe: strong recognition

editorialNotes.title: Note on grade placement
editorialNotes.text: Aligned 2026-08-20: this madde previously placed IGCSE one year later (Grades 10 to 11, with exams in the eleventh grade), extended A Level to a thirteenth grade, and put Checkpoint in the ninth grade. The network placement is: Checkpoint at the end of Grade 8, IGCSE across Grades 9-10 with May/June exams in Grade 10, AS Level taught in Grade 11, with the four AS examinations sat in the Grade 12 October/November series, and full A Level as an optional addition sat in the Grade 12 May/June series (corrected 2026-09-30 to the live Curriculum Module: Grades 11-12 Structure). A thirteenth grade does not exist in the Indonesian school structure.

content.text: Cambridge offers two main examination series each year. Eduversal Partner Schools usually use both series, depending on student needs.

Exam Period: Late April to Early June

Results Release: Early-Mid August

Typical Students:

items: Grade 10 students completing IGCSE (end of two-year course)
Any other registered May/June entries
Approved Grade 12 candidates who continue to the full A Level. They sit A Level in addition to the four AS examinations, never instead of them
content.title: May/June Series (IGCSE and Approved A Level Continuation Series)

content.text: Key Dates (Based on 2024-2025 cycle; confirm annually with Cambridge):

Exam Period: Late September to mid-November (subject/component-specific)

Results Release: Mid-January (following year)

Typical Students:

items: All Grade 12 students on the four-AS program (the Eduversal program-completion standard), plus students retaking exams to improve grades
Students who missed May/June because of illness or other reasons
A small number of students on faster or delayed timelines

items: Lower Secondary Checkpoint: every partner school enters its Grade 8 candidates in the May series. Using a different series needs the Academic Board's agreement in advance. (Primary Checkpoint follows the separate documents issued by the Primary Director.)
Trained school staff run the tests under Cambridge examination conditions and the published fixed timetable
Scripts sent to Cambridge for marking

content.text: Responsibility: Exams Officer, working with the Principal/GM, Academic Coordinators, and students/parents.

IGCSE Example (for students starting IGCSE in Grade 9, exams in Grade 10 May/June):

Process:

steps.text: Academic counseling sessions with students and parents
items: Review student strengths, interests, and university plans
Explain subject requirements and combinations
Discuss tier options (e.g., Mathematics Extended vs Core)
Students choose subjects from the school's offerings. The network default is six IGCSE subjects. Any lower load is a documented exception made after academic review
Prerequisite completion
Timetable feasibility
Teacher capacity

steps.text: The Exams Officer logs in to Cambridge International Direct
items: Portal for all Centre exam administration
Candidate name (as shown on passport or national ID)
Date of birth
Candidate number (given by Cambridge after first registration)
Subjects and syllabus codes
Tier (if this applies, e.g., Extended vs Core Mathematics)
Components (written papers, practical, coursework)

items: School Exam Timetable with rooms, seating plans, invigilation assignments

subsections.title: Secure Storage and Exam Materials Management

content.text: Principle: Exam papers are confidential until the exam starts. Key Time is not the start time. It is the point in each timetabled session when every candidate must be in the exam or under Full Centre Supervision. Cambridge sets the Key Time for the centre's location (Cambridge Handbook 2026, p.22). Breaches damage exam integrity and may lead to sanctions.

items: A lockable safe, cabinet or strong room kept just for exam materials

Limited access: two or three authorized key holders only - for example the Exams Officer, the Centre Head and one more trained member of staff. A key holder supervises anyone else in the secure room (Cambridge Handbook 2026, s.4.4)
The room has an alarm or is in a monitored area (e.g., the Principal's office or a secure admin room)
content.title: Secure Storage Requirements

items: Record every access to secure storage (date, time, person, purpose)
Keep the log for the whole exam period, and keep it afterwards for audit
Cambridge sends secure materials by tracked delivery
Exams Officer checks that the package is undamaged (seals intact, no damage)
Check contents against dispatch list
Sign and date receipt
Store immediately in secure location

content.text: Definition: The point in each timetabled session when every candidate must be in the exam or under Full Centre Supervision. Cambridge sets this point for the centre's location. It is not the start time. The centre chooses when each exam starts, as long as candidates are in the exam or supervised at the Key Time. Key Times do not apply to windowed exams (speaking tests, art & design, Checkpoint). Exam papers may not be opened or viewed by anyone before the exam starts. Adherence:

items: Exams Officer collects the sealed exam packets from secure storage as close to the start of the exam as possible. The packets are never left unattended
Two members of staff check the packet. The invigilator opens it in the exam room, in front of the candidates, at the start of the exam
Opening a packet late or early is malpractice and must be reported
content.title: Key Times

items: Each morning and afternoon session has its own Key Time, based on the centre's location. Check www.cambridgeinternational.org/keytimes before each series
Candidates are not allowed to leave before the Key Time

steps: Exams Officer takes the exam packet from secure storage
Transports to exam room (sealed)
Opens it in front of the invigilators and students at the start of the exam
Hands out the question papers and answer booklets
Invigilator checks that all students have the correct paper and materials
Exam starts
content.title: Exam Paper Distribution

items: Invigilator collects all scripts, question papers (if confidential), and unused materials
Return to Exams Officer immediately
Exams Officer keeps the scripts secure until they are sent to Cambridge

content.text: Purpose: To run exams fairly, securely and in line with Cambridge regulations, so that qualifications stay credible.

items: Teachers (from any subject, not just the exam subject)
Senior administrators
External invigilators (if school hires extra support)
content.title: Invigilator Qualifications

items: The teacher of the subject being examined in that exam (a conflict of interest; they may give hints without meaning to)
Close relatives of candidates sitting the exam
Students or untrained staff
All invigilators must complete Cambridge invigilation training (online module or school-based session)
Annual refresher required
Exams Officer gives a pre-exam briefing on the details of the exam and on backup plans
1 invigilator per 30 students
content.title: Invigilation Ratios

items: 1 invigilator for every 20-25 students, for closer supervision and faster answers to student questions
If there are more than 30 students, assign extra invigilators
Desks with enough space between them (minimum 1.25 meters between students to prevent copying)
Seating plan on display (each student has a set seat by candidate number)
Clock visible to all students
"Examination in Progress - Silence" signs on doors
content.title: Exam Room Setup

items: Mobile phones, smartwatches and other electronic devices (must be switched off and kept away from the exam area)
Unauthorized notes, books and dictionaries (unless Cambridge specifies them for open-book exams)
Calculators (only approved models on the Cambridge list are allowed)
Clear water bottle (label removed)
Pens, pencils, erasers, rulers (no cases with printed text)
Calculators (if allowed for subject)
Spec sheets and formula booklets (if Cambridge provides them)
Arrive 15 minutes before the exam starts
Present student ID or candidate number
Sit at the assigned seat
Follow all invigilator instructions
No communication with other students once the exam begins (no speaking, gestures or passing notes)
No cheating or malpractice (see Section 3.10)
content.title: Exam Conduct Rules

items: Arrive 30 minutes before the exam starts
Set up the room and check the materials
Check student IDs
Hand out the papers at the start of the exam
Watch students at all times (walk around the room quietly)
Answer student questions about the exam instructions (may explain how the exam works, but not its content)
Record start and end times
Collect all scripts and materials at the end of the exam
Report any irregularities immediately
Invigilators must stay alert and watchful
No reading, phone use, or other distractions by invigilators
If a student needs a restroom break (extended exams only): the invigilator escorts the student. No extra time is added unless it is a pre-approved accommodation
Candidates must be in the exam or under Full Centre Supervision at the Key Time. The centre sets each start time around it
Duration set by Cambridge (e.g., 1 hour 45 minutes, 2 hours 30 minutes)
5-minute warning before end
No extra time unless it is a pre-approved access arrangement
content.title: Exam Timing

items: If an exam starts late for an unavoidable reason (e.g., a fire alarm), contact Cambridge straight away for guidance
If a student has approved extra time (e.g., 25% extra), calculate it and apply it exactly

content.text: Cambridge provides fair access to exams for students with disabilities, learning differences, or temporary difficulties.
Purpose: Help students with long-term or permanent needs to show their abilities without disadvantage. Common Accommodations:

items: Extra time: up to 25% meets the needs of most candidates. Over 25% is possible where difficulties are very significant and persistent and the evidence supports it (see 8.6)
Supervised rest breaks
Scribe (someone writes down the answers the student dictates)
Reader (someone reads the questions aloud to the student)
Word processor (typing instead of handwriting)
Enlarged print papers
Modified paper format (e.g., Braille, audio)
content.title: Access Arrangements (Pre-Exam Accommodations)

items: Student must have a documented disability or learning difference (e.g., dyslexia, ADHD, visual impairment, physical disability)
An assessment by a qualified professional (educational psychologist, medical doctor) is required
Evidence of need in the normal classroom (the student uses the accommodation regularly, not just for exams)

content.title: Note
content.text: The deadline is given only in the key dates table in 10.3.

steps.text: Documentation Collection (at least 6 months before exams):
items: Parents provide diagnostic reports and professional recommendations
School EAL/SEN Coordinator reviews and confirms the need

steps.text: Application to Cambridge (by the access arrangements deadline in the key dates table, 10.3):
items: Exams Officer submits the Access Arrangement application through Cambridge International Direct
Include evidence (diagnostic reports, school support records)
Specify requested accommodation and rationale
Cambridge reviews it and either approves it or asks for extra information
Approval lasts for the student's whole time at the Centre (no need to re-apply each year unless the need changes)
Exams Officer makes sure the approved accommodations are in place for all relevant exams
A separate exam room if needed (e.g., for a student who uses a scribe or needs rest breaks)
Invigilator trained on specific accommodation
Access arrangement applications and approvals (stored securely for each student)
Implementation logs (which accommodations were used in which exams)
Student support records showing normal use of accommodations

content.text: Purpose: Let Cambridge consider circumstances that may have affected a student's performance for a short time. Examples:

items: Illness on exam day (the student took the exam but was unwell)
Bereavement (death of a close family member near the exam period)
Serious accident or trauma
Administrative error by the Centre (e.g., wrong paper given, timing error)
content.title: Special Considerations (Post-Exam Circumstances)

items: Exams Officer documents circumstances immediately
Student completes the exam if possible (or misses the exam if unable to sit it)

steps.text: Special Consideration Form (Cambridge Handbook 2026 p.117). Submit it no later than seven days after the LAST exam of the affected syllabus in that exam series. This is not seven days from the individual paper:
items: Exams Officer submits the form to Cambridge through Cambridge International Direct
Include evidence (medical certificate, incident report, other supporting documents)
Request consideration (this is not a request for a specific grade change; Cambridge decides)
Allow the script to be marked with consideration (a small grade adjustment is possible)
Declare the result void and let the student retake without penalty (rare)
Take no action if the circumstances are judged not to have had a significant effect on performance
Special consideration does not guarantee a change of grade
It does not replace the need for the student to sit the exam (unless this is physically impossible)
It must be applied for without delay (late applications are usually rejected)
Special consideration applications and outcomes
Supporting documentation (medical certificates, etc.)
Communication with Cambridge

editorialNotes.text: Updated 2026-08-20: this madde previously stated its own lead-time for access arrangement applications, which disagreed with Section 10. The deadline now lives only in the key dates table (10.3).

content.text: Definition: Any action that damages exam integrity or gives an unfair advantage.

items: Cheating: copying from another student, or using unauthorized notes or devices
Plagiarism: submitting coursework copied from the internet or other sources without citing them
Collusion: students working together on individual coursework and submitting the same or similar work
Personation: someone else taking the exam for a student, or a student taking the exam for someone else
Disruptive behavior: Deliberately disturbing other students
content.title: Types of Malpractice

items: Opening papers early: viewing a question paper before the exam starts
Inadequate security: Allowing unauthorized access to exam materials
Failure to report irregularities: the Centre knows about an issue but does not tell Cambridge
Providing unauthorized assistance: a teacher giving hints or answers during the exam
Falsifying coursework marks: a teacher raising marks unfairly for internal assessment
Academic integrity policy explained in the student handbook and in assemblies
Clear teaching of how to cite and reference sources in coursework
Consequences of malpractice clearly communicated
content.title: Prevention Strategies

items: Strictly following Cambridge storage and Key Time requirements
Multiple invigilators per room
Seating plans that reduce chances to copy
Prohibition of phones and electronics
Annual refresher on Cambridge conduct rules
Ethical standards emphasized
Reporting obligations clear
Invigilator sees suspicious behavior (looking at another paper, using a phone, etc.)
Invigilator reports it immediately to the Exams Officer
Incident recorded (time, student, behavior seen)
The student may be allowed to continue the exam while the incident is investigated (decision by Centre Head/Exams Officer)
content.title: Detection and Reporting

items: Cambridge notices similarity between scripts (similar unusual answers or errors)
Teacher or moderator notices plagiarism in coursework

Mandatory: the Head of Centre must tell Cambridge straight away about any suspected malpractice they become aware of or that is reported to them. There is no grace period and no 7-day window (Cambridge Handbook 2026 p.122, s.5.6.2)
Not reporting is itself malpractice by the Centre
Detailed description of incident
Evidence (invigilator statement, scripts, coursework samples)
Student statement (the Centre interviews the student; the student may admit or deny)
Centre recommendation (a sanction or further investigation)

steps: Cambridge reviews report and evidence
May ask the Centre or student for extra information
Decides whether malpractice happened or not
If malpractice confirmed, imposes sanction
content.title: Cambridge Investigation and Sanctions

items: Warning letter
Disqualification from the subject (no grade awarded)
Disqualification from all subjects in that series (all results cancelled)
Ban from future exams (1-5 years or permanent, depending on how serious it is)
Warning letter
Conditions placed on the Centre (closer monitoring, limits on coursework subjects)
Suspension of Centre status (for a time, the school is unable to register students)
Withdrawal of Centre status (permanent; the school can no longer offer Cambridge)
The student or Centre may appeal the Cambridge decision (Cambridge sets the process)
Incident reports for any irregularities or suspected malpractice
Correspondence with Cambridge regarding investigations
Sanctions imposed and follow-up actions

content.text: Timeline: Scripts must be sent to Cambridge on the day of the exam, or within five working days after it (Cambridge Handbook 2026) (or uploaded immediately if e-marking).

items: Invigilator collects all scripts and unused materials
Count the scripts (check that the number matches the student attendance register)
Return them to the Exams Officer in a sealed envelope
Exams Officer sorts the scripts by subject and syllabus code
Place them in Cambridge-provided packaging or a strong box
Complete the Attendance Register (a list of students who sat the exam, showing any absences)
Include any reports (special consideration forms, incident reports)
Send by approved courier (Cambridge provides a courier account or instructions)
Obtain tracking number
Retain proof of dispatch
Cambridge confirms receipt
Exams Officer tracks the shipment and follows up if it is delayed
Cambridge has moved many subjects to e-marking (check the yearly updates)
e-Marking: students write on paper as normal. The Centre scans the scripts and uploads them to Cambridge
content.title: e-Marking (Electronic Marking)

items: Use a high-quality scanner (Cambridge provides the specifications)
Scan each page of each student's script
Save as PDF
Upload the PDFs to Cambridge through the secure portal

Deadline: upload on the day of the exam wherever possible. The Cambridge deadline is five working days after the exam (late scripts risk NO RESULT / X grade). Eduversal internal target: 48 hours. (Cambridge Handbook 2026, s.5.4)
Cambridge reviews uploads for legibility
May request re-scan if quality not enough
Faster results
More efficient dispatch (no physical courier)
Reduced risk of lost scripts
The school must have enough scanning capacity and reliable internet
Staff training on scanning procedures
Attendance registers (retained by school for 5 years)
Dispatch receipts or upload confirmations
Tracking information
May/June series: results come out in early to mid August
Oct/Nov series: Results released mid-January
content.title: Results Release

items: Centre Head and Exams Officer log in to Cambridge International Direct
Download Statement of Results (PDF listing all students' grades)
Individual candidate statements are available to print
The school gives results to students (at a results day event, by email, or on the student portal)
Confidentiality: results are shared only with the student and parents (not posted publicly)

items.text: Exams Officer and Principal/GM analyze results:
items: Overall pass rates and grade distribution
Subject-level performance
Comparison with previous years and with international benchmarks (if Cambridge provides them)
Identify strengths and areas for improvement (use them in the School Improvement Plan)
Cambridge sends certificates about 3 months after results are released
Certificates are sent to the Centre (not directly to students)
content.title: Certificates

items: The school holds a ceremony to present certificates (usually at graduation or a special awards event)
Certificates are given to students in a sealed envelope
Student signs register confirming receipt
If a certificate is lost or damaged, the student may ask Cambridge for a replacement (a fee applies)
The school keeps a copy of results for its records (certificates belong to students)

content.text: Students or parents may ask for a review of results if they believe there is an error.
content.title: Post-Results Services

content.text: Purpose: To ask Cambridge to re-check the marking or to return the marked script for review. Services Available:

items: Clerical re-check: A check that all questions were marked and the marks were added up correctly (no re-marking; just a check for administrative errors)
Re-moderation of coursework: For subjects with a coursework component, an external moderator reviews the Centre's marking again
Return of scripts: The student receives a photocopy of the marked script to see the examiner's comments (no grade change; for learning purposes)
Priority re-mark: A senior examiner fully re-marks the script (the grade may go up or down)
content.title: 1. Enquiries About Results (EARs)

items: Set by Cambridge for each series: a short window after results are released. See 10.7.2 (post-results services) and the key dates table in 10.3
Submit promptly - late requests are not accepted

content.title: Note
content.text: The deadline is given only in Section 10.

steps: The student or parent requests an EAR (Enquiry About Results) and pays the fee. The fee goes to the school or directly to Cambridge, depending on school policy
The Exams Officer submits the EAR through Cambridge International Direct
Cambridge processes (2-4 weeks)
The outcome is communicated (the grade stays the same, goes up, or goes down)

items: If a re-mark changes the grade (up or down), Cambridge issues a revised certificate
Revised grade is final
EAR requests and outcomes logged
Communication with students and parents about the process and fees
Revised certificates (if grades changed)
Analysis of EAR outcomes (look for any patterns that show teaching or assessment needs to improve)

content.text: Purpose: To let students see their marked exam scripts for learning, even if they do not request a re-mark. Process:

items: The student requests access to scripts (a fee applies)
Cambridge provides scanned copies with examiner marks and comments
No grade change; it is just for feedback
content.title: 2. Access to Scripts

items: Teachers review the scripts with students to find strengths and areas for improvement
Inform future exam preparation strategies
If the student believes Cambridge made a procedural error (something other than marking accuracy)
Examples: the wrong exam was given, special consideration was not applied properly, or a malpractice sanction was unjust
content.title: 3. Appeals

items: A formal appeal to Cambridge, with detailed reasons and evidence
Cambridge Appeals Panel reviews
Decision typically final
Support the student with documents if the appeal has merit
Stay neutral (do not act as the student's advocate, but help make the process fair)

content.text: Purpose: To make sure the school's assessment practices match Cambridge standards. This matters most for subjects with coursework or teacher-assessed components.

items: Art & Design: Portfolio of work assessed by teacher
Sciences: Practical skills assessed during course
English Literature: Some syllabi include a coursework essay
content.title: Subjects with Coursework/Teacher Assessment

items: Use the mark schemes and assessment criteria that Cambridge provides
Give marks for each student's coursework
The Department Head or an experienced teacher reviews a sample of marked work
Consistency (work of similar quality gets similar marks)
Accuracy (marks align with criteria)
Rank order (students are placed in the correct order of performance)
Discuss any differences and adjust marks if needed
The Exams Officer uploads teacher-assessed marks through Cambridge International Direct
The deadline is usually 1-2 months before the written exams
Cambridge chooses a sample of students' work for the Centre to submit (often from the highest, middle and lowest achieving students)
A Cambridge moderator reviews the Centre's marks and compares them with the moderator's own independent assessment
If there is a difference, Cambridge may adjust all marks for that subject up or down to match the standard
Teacher marks are combined with external exam marks (Cambridge sets the weighting)
Final grade issued
Before assessing coursework or internal assessments
At the start of each marking period
content.title: Standardization Meetings

items: Make sure all teachers of the same subject understand and use mark schemes in the same way

steps: Teachers review mark schemes and assessment criteria together
Mark sample student work independently
Compare marks and discuss differences
Reach consensus on standards
Document agreement

items: Standardization meeting agendas and notes
Sample marked work (with notes showing the marks and the reasons for them)
Internal moderation reports
External moderation feedback from Cambridge

content.text: Purpose: To help teachers deliver high-quality Cambridge curriculum and assessment.

items: Cambridge Professional Development Qualification (PDQ): Teaching & Learning; Leadership
Cambridge International Certificate in Teaching and Learning: Subject-specific (e.g., Teaching Mathematics)
Online courses: Self-paced modules on Cambridge teaching methods, assessment and specific subjects
content.title: Cambridge Professional Development Qualifications

items: Eduversal pays part or all of the cost of Cambridge PD (professional development) for key staff
Target: All HODs (Heads of Department) and core subject teachers complete at least one Cambridge PD qualification
Tracked via HR professional development records
Access is through login details (each Centre has access)
Syllabi and specimen papers: Current and past exam papers with mark schemes
Schemes of Work: Suggested teaching sequences and lesson plans
Teacher Guides: Detailed guidance on teaching methods and assessment
Learner Guides: Resources for students
Past Papers: Earlier exams for practice

items: Teachers download resources for planning and teaching
Students access past papers for exam preparation
The school may buy extra resources (textbooks, online platforms like Cambridge GO)
Records of Cambridge PD course completion

Student exam preparation materials (past papers, practice tests)
Cambridge offers free webinars throughout the year on curriculum updates, assessment and teaching methods
Recorded sessions are available to watch later

items: Occasional face-to-face workshops in Indonesia or the region (Jakarta, Singapore)

Monitors Cambridge training opportunities
Shares information with staff
Encourages participation

content.text: Purpose: A recognition program for schools that show excellence in Cambridge education. Award Levels:

items: Registered: School applies and commits to the development plan
Accredited: The school meets quality benchmarks in teaching, assessment and student support
Outstanding: Highest level; exemplary practice
External validation of quality
Marketing advantage (logo, certificate)
Access to exclusive Cambridge resources and events
Professional development opportunities

Conduct self-assessment against award criteria
Submit evidence portfolio
Cambridge reviews and awards the right level

Cambridge International School Award application and status

Award certificate and renewal tracking

content.title: Key Cambridge Policies (Schools Must Follow):

items: Cambridge requires all Centres to have a child protection policy
Students taking exams must be in a safe environment
Duties to report if safeguarding concerns come up
Student data shared with Cambridge must be secure
Cambridge complies with GDPR (UK/EU data laws); Centres must follow local laws (Indonesia's PDP Law)
Cambridge owns the copyright of exam questions and materials
Schools may not copy or share exam papers publicly (except past papers that Cambridge has released)
Breaking this rule is a breach of the Centre agreement

content.text: 5. Marketing and Use of Cambridge Name:

items: Schools may state that they are a Cambridge Centre
Schools may use the Cambridge logo with permission
Schools may not give a false picture of their relationship with Cambridge (e.g., they cannot claim to be "Cambridge University-affiliated")
All marketing materials mentioning Cambridge must be accurate

items: Chosen at random or based on Centre performance data
Advance notice (typically 4-6 weeks)
Focus: Facilities, exam security, staff training, student support

More intensive scrutiny
Before Cambridge gives Centre status to a new school
Verify application information
Exam rooms (capacity, seating, lighting, noise control)

Accessibility (accommodations for students with disabilities)

Provide requested documents promptly
